actual_scope: Exhaustive census of the c=1 signed-permutation stabilizer on the trivial-character (+1,+1) 216-space, deciding which elements outside the normalizer of {g,t} preserve that space and act non-scalarly.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for a formal caller or certificate binding. The assigned question, taken from the outside-normalizer clause of open PR #7008, asks whether any signed permutation in the c=1 stabilizer outside the normalizer of {g,t} preserves the trivial-character (+1,+1) 216-space and acts non-scalarly. PR #7008's stored second question asks the analogous question for the 8-dimensional isotypic summand. This package answers the 216-dimensional preservation question. It does not add a Lean binding, does not decide the 8-dimensional question, and does not change kappa.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result on the historical centre Gram. The selected conditional kappa remains 781451/250000000. Further lifts of the same dihedral image do not replace the degree-881 one-slot annihilator and do not admit a supplier.
stop_rule: Stop once every c=1 stabilizer element has been tested for preservation of the ++ 216-space and one explicit outside non-scalar witness has been checked against the normalizer. Do not build the 8-dimensional projector and do not rerun the degree-881 certificate.
evidence: verify.py enumerates the line-preserving signed permutations and all 3072 c=1 stabilizer elements. Marker PASS_C1_216_OUTSIDE_NORMALIZER. The ++ space has 768 preservers. Of the 672 outside the normalizer, 560 act non-scalarly, and the image in GL(E) still has order 12. The witness is u times the coordinate-1 sign, with trace 72. Selected baseline returned PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY.

open_questions.question: Does any c=1 stabilizer element that moves the ++ 216-space preserve the 8-dimensional dihedral isotypic summand and act non-scalarly on it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR #7008 asks whether an element outside the normalizer preserves that 8-dimensional summand and acts non-scalarly. Under the linear-character identification recorded there, every element that preserves the ambient 216-space acts through the same dihedral image and therefore by a scalar on that summand. A non-scalar action would have to come from an element that moves the 216-space.
open_questions.first_step: Apply the multiplicity-8 dihedral projector to one c=1 stabilizer element whose projector correlation with the 216-space is 0, and test whether the 8-dimensional image is invariant with restricted trace not equal to ±8.
open_questions.blocked_by: The trace on the ambient 4096-dimensional block does not decide invariance of that summand. This package does not build the projector image.

open_questions.question: Is the 8-dimensional isotypic summand irreducible under A_1?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the smallest rational A_1-invariant subspace the signed-permutation normalizer isolates inside the 216-space. A scalar signed-permutation action does not decide irreducibility under A_1.
open_questions.first_step: Build a basis of the image of the integer projector for the multiplicity-8 character and decide whether the restricted block has a proper invariant subspace.
open_questions.blocked_by: The character inner product certifies the dimension without listing a basis. This census does not construct that basis.

overlap.limits: Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, TASK metadata and the ledger. No code diffs. The phrases 216-dimensional summand, non-scalarly, and normalizer of match PR #7008, which leaves the outside-normalizer question open, and do not match another open PR that answers it.
